key_idea: Every T has length >= 2 so expansions at least double per step: after about 50 steps a single character already covers 1e15 positions, so only the first character of f^(K-60)(S) matters and it follows a functional graph on 26 letters.
sketch: Let D=min(K,60) and compute len[d][c] = |f^d(c)| capped at 4e18 by DP. If K<=60 the base string is S; otherwise the base is the single character obtained by iterating c -> T_c[0] exactly K-60 times starting from S[0], done with cycle detection on the 26-node functional graph. For a query, binary search capped prefix sums of len[D] over the base string to find the character, then descend D levels, at each level scanning T_c to find which child contains the offset: O(D*50) per query. Pitfalls: saturate lengths to avoid overflow, K up to 1e15 so never iterate K steps, off-by-one between 1-based positions and offsets. Stress-tested against direct simulation for small K and against a first-character simulation for K>60.
